Medjat Lexicon

Look up a word across several dictionaries at once, from Yorùbá and Lucumí to Kikongo, the Kongo of Cuba, Kimbundu, Twi, and the African vocabulary of Brazilian Portuguese. Type it with or without tone marks and underdots: Ṣàngó, Sango, Changó and Shango all find each other. Every entry names its dictionary, and older sources link to the printed page.

About the sources

Connections between languages run through English meanings. Spanish, French and Portuguese definitions reach English through WikDict bilingual dictionaries, built from Wiktionary and licensed Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike; links marked "via translation" depend on them. Modern standard forms and their glosses come from Wiktionary (via kaikki.org), Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike. Standard definitions come from Open English WordNet (CC BY 4.0), with scientific names and modern names from Wikidata (CC0); IHS corrects WordNet where it misdescribes Afro-Atlantic practice, and gives no standard definition where a source uses missionary vocabulary. Page images of the older dictionaries are served by the Internet Archive.

Built . Older dictionaries were read by OCR and have not all been reviewed; an entry marked OCR, unreviewed should be checked against the page image before it is cited.
